meta.parties: Muhseen Et Al. v. Habeeb Et Al

rules.statement: A Muslim dowry deed promising to pay something not yet in existence (in futuro) is valid under the ordinary law of Ceylon, even if governed by Muslim law.
rules.supporting_quote: "This however does not seem to be correct. In 2 Ameer Ali 440 (5th ed.) we read 'Munaf'a (profits accruing from land investments, business, industry, &c.) . . . . are proper subjects of dower'. Tyabji 171 (2nd ed.) says 'The rents and profits of property . . . . may validly be the subject of mahr', i.e., dower. These passages refer, certainly, to dower given or promised to the wife by the husband: does it make any difference that here it is dower given or promised by the wife's parents? There seems no reason why it should."
